comparison: Perfect agreement on C25-C27 regarding localization independence. Both evaluations find the microscopy data (Figures 1A, 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) fully support that neither Dbp5 nor Los1/Msn5 localization depends on the other. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on C28-C33 regarding genetic evidence for parallel pathways. Both evaluations accept the spot assays and tRNA FISH data showing additive defects in double mutants as strong evidence for independent pathways. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Disagreement on C34-C37 regarding RNA IP data showing Dbp5-tRNA interaction in los1Δ. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, noting the ~2-fold reduction suggests Los1 may facilitate but is not required. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, noting the decreased interaction 'suggests that the idea of these pathways in parallel may be too simplistic' and questions the interpretation.

Perfect agreement on C38-C40 regarding direct Dbp5-tRNA interaction independent of Mex67. Both evaluations accept the RNA IP data (Figures 2B-C) and the distinction from mRNA binding mechanisms. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on claims about Gle1-dependent ATPase activation. OpenEval R5 covers C41-C48 (mutant characterization and northern blot data), rating SUPPORTED. Peer R5 focuses only on C47-C48 (Gle1 dependence), also rating SUPPORTED. Both agree on Gle1's role but OpenEval includes broader mutant characterization.

Overlap on C41-C46 regarding characterization of dbp5 mutants from prior literature. OpenEval R5 includes these as part of broader evaluation of northern blot data. Peer R13 separately evaluates these literature-based characterizations. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on C51-C55 regarding direct Dbp5-tRNA binding demonstrated by EMSA and fluorescence polarization. Both evaluations accept the in vitro binding data and quantitative measurements. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on C49-C50 regarding nucleotide-state dependence of Dbp5 binding from literature. OpenEval R6 includes these as context for current EMSA data. Peer R14 groups these with other literature background. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on C56-C57 regarding lack of tRNA-stimulated ATPase activity. OpenEval R7 focuses only on these claims. Peer R7 combines C56-C57 with C58-C64 (Gle1/InsP6 requirement). Both agree on the findings and rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on C58-C64 regarding Gle1/InsP6-dependent ATPase activation by tRNA. OpenEval R8 focuses on these claims with detailed quantitative analysis. Peer R7 combines these with C56-C57. Both emphasize the synergistic activation and spatial regulation at NPCs. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on C66-C67 regarding additive genetic interactions between Dbp5 and Gle1 mutants with los1Δ. Both evaluations accept the northern blot data showing parallel pathway function. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on C68-C70, the main conclusions synthesizing all findings. Both evaluations affirm the overall model of Dbp5 functioning in parallel with Los1/Msn5, dependent on Gle1, with direct tRNA binding. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on C65, C72-C73, C80, C83, C87, C90 as speculative mechanistic interpretations. Both evaluations recognize these as hypotheses rather than demonstrated mechanisms. Both rate as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging they are consistent with data but require future testing.
Perfect agreement on C1-C19 as established background knowledge from published literature. Both evaluations accept these context-setting claims without question. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
Perfect agreement on C20-C24 regarding prior work from Lari et al., 2019 that motivated the current study. Both evaluations accept this published foundation. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on C74-C75 and other discussion claims drawing on literature. OpenEval R14 groups C74-C96 (excluding speculative claims) as literature-supported discussion. Peer R14 focuses on C49-C50, C71, C74-C75 as established biochemical properties. Both rate overlapping claims as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on C76-C79, C84-C86 regarding established mRNA export model. OpenEval R14 includes these in broader discussion grouping. Peer R15 separately evaluates these as accepted background for comparison. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on C88-C89, C91-C94, C96 regarding broader implications. OpenEval R14 groups these with other discussion claims. Peer R16 focuses on broader significance and coordination of RNA export. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Partial overlap on C81-C82, C95, C97-C100 regarding broader implications and future directions. OpenEval R15 notes C95 and C97 contain speculative elements but rates overall as SUPPORTED. Peer R16 affirms broader significance of coordinated RNA export. Both rate as SUPPORTED.
